mount-hood.description: Oregon’s highest mountain is an iconic Cascade volcano whose upper slopes demand technical snow-and-ice travel. A summit attempt is a serious alpine objective, with conditions that can change quickly and hazards including falling ice, crevasses and avalanches.
highlights: Views across Oregon and Washington on clear days
mount-hood.whatToKnow: Mount Hood climbing permits are required for travel above 9,500 feet. Review current Forest Service climbing reports, weather, avalanche information and route requirements before planning any ascent.

washington-park.description: Washington Park brings together major gardens, forest paths, cultural destinations and the Oregon Zoo in Portland’s West Hills. The park rewards both a short wander and a day of exploring, with several distinct Quested discoveries within its boundaries.
washington-park.whatToKnow: Parking can be limited. The MAX light rail serves Washington Park, and a seasonal shuttle connects attractions. Check each destination’s visiting requirements separately.

forest-park.description: Forest Park offers a sweeping network of wooded trails and quiet ravines just beyond Portland’s urban core. The Wildwood Trail anchors a landscape of forest walks, trail runs and wildlife habitat.
highlights: Numerous entry points and route options
forest-park.whatToKnow: Choose an appropriate trailhead and route; surfaces and elevation changes vary. Check Portland Parks trail alerts for closures and storm damage before you go.

powell-butte-nature-park.description: An extinct cinder cone in southeast Portland, Powell Butte mixes broad grassy meadows with forest and a network of trails. On a clear day, its open terrain invites expansive views toward the Cascades.
powell-butte-nature-park.whatToKnow: Stay on designated routes and keep dogs leashed. The main entrance or parking gate may close during freezing conditions.

mount-tabor-park.description: Mount Tabor rises from southeast Portland on an extinct volcanic cinder cone, blending mature trees, stairways, scenic overlooks and historic reservoirs. It is an approachable place for a sunset walk or an urban hill workout.
mount-tabor-park.whatToKnow: Some roads are closed to vehicles at designated times, and ongoing construction may affect a few paths. Check park updates before visiting.

council-crest-park.description: Council Crest sits high above southwest Portland and opens up sweeping views of the city and surrounding landscape. On clear days, Cascade mountains punctuate the horizon.
council-crest-park.whatToKnow: Vehicle access hours are seasonal; the park can be visited on foot beyond the vehicle gate. Check posted access and weather conditions.

rocky-butte-natural-area.description: Rocky Butte is another remnant of Portland’s volcanic past. Its forested slopes rise to a hilltop viewpoint at Joseph Wood Hill Park, with an unusual mix of geology, city history and skyline views.
rocky-butte-natural-area.whatToKnow: Vehicle access near the summit is seasonally restricted, and parking regulations vary. Review city park notices before visiting.

pittock-mansion.description: Pittock Mansion and its surrounding park offer a memorable perspective on Portland and the Cascade skyline. The landmark is also accessible from several Forest Park trail routes, connecting urban history with an outdoor adventure.
pittock-mansion.whatToKnow: Mansion admission and park access are separate experiences. Parking arrangements and visiting hours can change; confirm details with the official park or attraction before visiting.

mount-adams-circumnavigation.description: Circle Mount Adams on an advanced route combining established paths and cross-country sections. The mountain does not have a continuous maintained trail loop; Yakama Nation lands have separate access regulations.
highlights: Complete a full circuit rather than a summit visit
Experience multiple sides of the landscape
mount-adams-circumnavigation.whatToKnow: Off-trail navigation is required. Check closures, permits and Yakama Nation access rules before route planning; do not assume all potential sections are open.

mount-st-helens-circumnavigation.description: Complete the Loowit Trail circuit around Mount St. Helens, crossing rugged gullies, volcanic plains and exposed landscapes. A full circuit is different from hiking a shorter Loowit segment.
highlights: Complete a full circuit rather than a summit visit
Experience multiple sides of the landscape
mount-st-helens-circumnavigation.whatToKnow: Check current WTA and Forest Service closures, campsites, access rules, water and terrain changes. Washouts and stream crossings can be serious obstacles.

mount-jefferson-circumnavigation.description: A full circuit of Mount Jefferson is a demanding cross-country challenge, not a designated or continuous maintained hiking loop. It requires careful independent route research.
highlights: Complete a full circuit rather than a summit visit
Experience multiple sides of the landscape
mount-jefferson-circumnavigation.whatToKnow: Complex terrain, snow, drainage crossings, wildfire damage, closures, permits and access can affect feasibility. This is a challenge concept, not navigation guidance.

mount-hood-circumnavigation.description: Circle Mount Hood on the famous Timberline Trail, passing alpine meadows, forests, ridgelines and glacial drainages. A full loop is separate from a summit ascent.
highlights: Complete a full circuit rather than a summit visit
Experience multiple sides of the landscape
mount-hood-circumnavigation.whatToKnow: Glacial stream crossings may be dangerous and conditions change rapidly. Check current trail conditions, weather, closures and permits.

crater-lake-circumnavigation.eyebrow: Rim circuit · No continuous hiking trail
crater-lake-circumnavigation.description: Crater Lake offers spectacular rim viewpoints and short trails, but the NPS does not describe a continuous designated hiking trail for a full on-foot circumnavigation. This is a complex, self-planned concept, not a verified hiking route.
highlights: Complete a full circuit rather than a summit visit
Experience multiple sides of the landscape
crater-lake-circumnavigation.whatToKnow: Do not assume Rim Drive is a safe or permitted pedestrian trail or that cross-country travel is allowed. Verify any planned route, restrictions and traffic safety directly with the National Park Service.

three-fingered-jack-circumnavigation.description: A loop around Three Fingered Jack connects the Pacific Crest Trail and other trails, passing lakes, meadows and volcanic viewpoints. It does not require climbing the exposed summit.
highlights: Complete a full circuit rather than a summit visit
Experience multiple sides of the landscape
three-fingered-jack-circumnavigation.whatToKnow: Confirm the specific loop variant and its trail junctions, access conditions, snow, water and applicable Central Cascades Wilderness permits.

living-blindly.description: Three-pitch bolted climb on the Marsupials with exposed moves and a memorable summit. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: Three pitches on Smith Rock’s Marsupials
Exposed movement and a memorable finish
A true multipitch objective with descent logistics
living-blindly.whatToKnow: Requires practiced lead belaying, multipitch anchor transitions, and safe rappelling or other verified descent. The optional ridge traverse is exposed and unprotected; do not assume it is part of an easy descent. Check access and conditions.

first-kiss.description: Five-pitch bolted adventure with traversing pitches and a scenic walk-off. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: Five pitches on Kiss of the Lepers Buttress
A summit finish and walk-off descent
first-kiss.whatToKnow: Communication and rope drag on traverses can complicate belays. The standard descent involves exposed scrambling and walking off, not simply rappelling the route. Check current Smith Rock raptor nesting closures.

santiam-pinnacle-south-face.description: Three-pitch sport route up an andesite pinnacle near Santiam Pass. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: Three pitches to a distinct summit
Short approach from the highway corridor
Mossy lower terrain and exposed upper slabs
santiam-pinnacle-south-face.whatToKnow: The lower pitches can be mossy and protection may be difficult to spot. Descent requires confirming the correct rappel anchors, rope length, and current hardware. Inspect all anchors independently.

giants-staircase.description: Two-pitch bolted route to the summit of French's Dome, with an airy rappel. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
giants-staircase.whatToKnow: Route descriptions distinguish a moderate traverse from a steeper 5.10 variation; choose carefully. Missing-anchor-hardware reports were posted in August 2026, followed by an update that repairs were made. Independently verify current anchors, rappel stations, and route access before climbing.

poppys-peril.description: Five-pitch bolted climbing above the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Valley. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: Five pitches and a substantial outing
poppys-peril.whatToKnow: Five pitches demand reliable transitions, route reading, partner communication, and descent planning. Verify current approach, anchors, closures, weather and local climbing reports before setting out.

cobbles-101.description: Five-pitch sport climbing on cobble-studded volcanic rock in Washington's southern Cascades. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: Five pitches on distinctive volcanic rock
Views toward several Pacific Northwest volcanoes
cobbles-101.whatToKnow: Pinto Rock is in Gifford Pinchot National Forest. Remote road access, variable rock quality and descent requirements merit extra planning. Confirm open forest roads, route-specific protection and anchor conditions before travel.

cocaine-connection.description: Two-pitch bolted slab and friction climbing on Icicle Buttress. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: A route with distinctive traversing movement
cocaine-connection.whatToKnow: Slab friction and traversing demand attentive rope management. The route reference discusses unusual rope requirements for some rappels; plan the descent from up-to-date route information and verify seasonal access and raptor notices.

voyage-of-the-cowdog.description: Three-pitch sport route on Picnic Lunch Wall with an airy final pitch. A featured objective in Quested’s Northwest Moderate Multipitch Classics collection.
highlights: Three-pitch journey on Picnic Lunch Wall
voyage-of-the-cowdog.whatToKnow: The route has reports of loose rock and a more complex descent than the grade suggests. Rappels are especially sensitive to rope length; consider the established walk-off after reviewing current route information. Smith Rock may impose seasonal raptor closures.
